what_this_is: What has been run and what has not, recomputed from the files that would know. Nothing here is maintained by hand: a figure that goes stale in this file is a figure that was never read from its source.
why_it_exists: No tracked file said what the state of the project was, so several said part of it in their own words and went stale apart from one another. The audit of 2026-09-15 prescribed this file and it was not built; the audit of 2026-10-21 found stale claims across the tracked documents, every one of them a symptom of its absence. How many is not stated here: this file carried the figure 42 by hand, no artefact holds it, and three of those findings were not false claims at all. What the audit says now is in `claims_audit`, which is read from its report.
what_it_does_not_say: Whether an instrument is valid, whether a measurement would be any good, and whether anybody outside this project has agreed to anything. It reports what has happened, not what it is worth.

searches.what_the_logs_hold: each run query's date, its record count and the sha256 of its export; the numbers stay there rather than being restated here

literature.what_reading_is_not: Every reading recorded there is the assistant's. Nobody has checked a quote against its paper, which is why the last figure is zero and is reported beside the others rather than instead of them.

translation.chosen_by: a back-translation check over 40 turns against gpt-oss-120b, recorded before use
translation.what_this_is_not: Two conversations are a feasibility pilot's materials and not a cohort. No note has been written from them by generation 2.

review_decisions.what_delegated_means: The investigator reviewed the criteria once and delegated the rest; a delegated decision is the assistant's and is recorded as such.

claims_audit.what_it_reports: Every published claim the checker can decide, against the file that holds it, with the live findings listed first. A live count of zero is not a clean repository: four classes of defect are found by reading and the report names them.
claims_audit.why_no_number_here: The audit scans this file, so a count copied into it would decide the next run's answer and neither artefact could be built first. The figure lives in the audit's own report, which tests/test_state.py holds to a fresh run, and the 42 this file used to carry was typed in and checkable nowhere.

generation_1.rows_are_not_notes: A row is one scored question of one note by one judge, so the row count is not a count of notes, and the two figures above are why: a row id repeats and a row can carry no scored session at all. Neither of them is a count of notes either, and this file does not report one, because the ledger does not hold it.

generation_2.what_that_means: Nothing from generation 2 has been scored into the result ledger. Its operational rules are a proposal; a sentence in the present tense about one of its measurements describes a plan, not a result.
generation_2.what_this_does_not_establish: That no note exists. Generation 2 writes notes into a workspace store through packages/therapy-note-eval-core pipeline.py, and that store is gitignored, so this file reports the silence of results/rows.jsonl and not the absence of a note. The protocol's pilot status, quoted under protocol below, is the tracked statement that the round has not run.

catalog.catalog_status: AI-authored proposals from the scoping search of 2026-09-13, translated to English by the coding assistant on 2026-09-16. No human acceptance decision exists for any entry; the executable registry is derived from this catalog only as a draft that the core refuses to freeze until humans review it.

panel.registration_status_as_the_protocol_stat: registered before any rating exists; no answer has been collected and no sheet has been sent. The pool was 34 items when the rule was registered and is larger now; catalog/catalog.json holds the list the sheet is built from, and the sheet takes its count from that list rather than stating one.
panel.note: Nothing here is read from local/panel/, where the sheets are built. That directory is gitignored, so what it holds differs between machines and a state file that reported it would not be the same file twice. Whether a sheet has been sent and whether an answer exists are quoted from the protocol's own registration above, which is tracked and is the one place to correct if it is wrong.
